tags.name: Resilience
tags.description:
Resilience exposes the high-availability state of the proxies (circuit breaker status and effective
settings) and manages automatic failover policies and the history of performed failovers.

tags.name: Webhook
tags.description:
Webhook service receives storage events and enqueues replication tasks.
Returns non-200 only on transient errors (context cancelled, Redis
unavailable) where a retry may succeed. Permanent errors (unknown storage,
invalid events, no replication policy) are logged server-side and return 200.

post.summary:
Schedules downtime window to switch source<->destination replication
targets. See SwitchDowntimeOpts for downtime scheduling options.
Can be edited if downtime window has not started yet.
post.description:
During downtime window all requests to replication target are blocked on
chorus proxy. When all replication tasks are processed, chorus can perform
optional data equality check and complete the switch. On completion, proxy
unblocks requests to target and routes all requests to destination target.

Unlike zero-downtime switch, downtime switch can perform optional data
equality check and rollback to source target without data loss.
Requirements:
  - replication must exist
  - replication must be proxy-based (agent replication is not supported)
  - for bucket-level replication, from/to bucket names must be the same
  - switch is not started. Use DeleteBucketSwitch in this case.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:

with downtime window.

post.summary:
Deletes Switch with following implications:
!!!Use with caution for ZeroDowntime switch.
post.description:
- [OK] If switch was in not_started, error, or skipped state, it will not
be attempted anymore. Routing will not be affected.
- If switch was in_progress, it will be aborted:
     * [OK] For downtime switch, block will be removed and proxy will
     route all requests to source target, no data will be lost.
     * [WARN] For ZeroDowntime switch, routing will be reverted back to
     source target. Meaning that targets may end up in inconsistent state
     because some writes were already routed to destination target.
- [OK] If switch was done. Only switch metadata will be removed,
replication or routing will not be affected.

post.summary:
Switches source<->destination replication targets without downtime.
Zero-downtime switch will take effect immediately on chorus proxy:
- all writes will be now routed to replication destination
- all reads will be routed to target with latest data
When all replication tasks will be processed, switch will be completed and
all reads and writes will be routed to destination target only.
post.description:
Unlike switch with downtime, zero-downtime switch is not checking bucket
contents on completion and cannot be aborted or reverted without risk of
data loss.
Requirements for zero-downtime switch:
  - replication must exist
  - replication must be proxy-based (agent replication is not supported)
  - for bucket-level replication, from/to bucket names must be the same
  - no existing switch must exist for given replication. Zero downtime
  switch cannot be updated. Use DeleteBucketSwitch in this case.

get.summary:
ListConsoleUsers returns the users able to sign in to the management API: config users (read-only) and
managed users stored in Redis. Never returns password hashes. Admin only.

post.summary: CreateConsoleUser creates a managed console user with a given or a generated (returned once) password.

put.summary: UpdateConsoleUser changes the role and/or the disabled flag of a managed user. Sessions are affected immediately.
DeleteConsoleUser removes a managed user. Its sessions stop working immediately.

ResetConsoleUserPassword sets or generates a new password of a managed user, forces a password change at the
next login and revokes all sessions of the user.

get.summary: ListFailoverEvents returns the performed failovers that were not yet cleared.

post.summary:
SetFailoverPolicy creates or replaces the failover policy of a source storage.
Source and targets must be configured storages.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: FailoverPolicy defines which storages may be promoted when the source storage is down.

put.summary: DeleteFailoverPolicy removes the failover policy of a source storage.

get.summary:
GetProxyStatus returns all live proxy instances with the health of their storages and effective settings.
Proxies publish their status periodically; an instance that stopped publishing disappears after a short TTL.

ListProxyAccounts returns the accounts able to authenticate against live proxies (users of storage credentials
used by the proxy and custom credentials) with their effective access policy. Secrets are never returned.
Runtime-managed ("dynamic") accounts are listed with source "dynamic" and their lifecycle metadata.

post.summary:
CreateProxyAccount creates a runtime-managed proxy account for an existing storage user and returns the
generated access key id and secret. The secret is returned ONLY in this response.
Fails with FailedPrecondition if the dynamic credentials master password is not configured.

put.summary: DeleteProxyAccount permanently removes a dynamic account.

RotateProxyAccountSecret generates a new secret. The previous secret keeps working for grace_period.
The new secret is returned ONLY in this response.
SetProxyAccountStatus enables ("active") or disables ("disabled") a dynamic account.

get.summary:
GetStatsHistory returns the traffic rates of all proxies over the last `range` (5m, 15m, 1h or 6h), summed
across proxies per time bucket (10s; 30s for 1h; 2m for 6h), plus the latest rates of every proxy.
Proxies record a sample every 10s into Redis (kept 6h), so history survives UI reloads.

ListS3Users returns the union of all users across storages with the credential state per storage (never the
secret), the proxy access key counts and the access policy summary.

post.summary:
CreateS3User creates a user with dynamic credentials on the given storages (the main storage is required),
optionally verifying them first, setting an access policy and creating the first proxy access key.
Fails with FailedPrecondition if dynamic credentials are not enabled. Partial changes are rolled back.

put.summary:
UpdateS3UserCredentials sets or replaces the dynamic credentials of an existing user on one storage.
Credentials defined in the worker config cannot be changed (FailedPrecondition).

DeleteS3User removes the dynamic credentials, dynamic proxy access keys and the access policy of a user.
Refused with FailedPrecondition (listing all reasons) if any credentials come from config or if replications,
routings or failover events reference the user. Active access keys also block deletion unless force is set.

post.summary:
TestS3UserCredentials checks credentials against one storage with a ListBuckets call.
Uses the given credentials or, if not given, the stored credentials of the user.

S3Notifications receives standard AWS S3 notification events and enqueues
replication tasks. Compatible with S3 bucket notification push format.
Events that cannot be processed are skipped and logged server-side.

parameters.name: storage
parameters.description: Chorus storage alias (must be a configured S3 storage). Bound to URL path.

post.summary:
SwiftEvents receives a batch of OpenStack Swift events parsed from
access logs by an external log exporter (e.g. Fluent Bit, Vector)
and enqueues replication tasks for events matching active policies.
Events that cannot be processed are skipped and logged server-side.

chorusEventSource.description:
Determines how ongoing data change events are captured for replication.

pointing to its own webhook endpoint. Bucket-level replication only.

Requires webhook to be enabled in worker config. No automatic setup.

Approximate time lag for syncing events to destination.
Corresponds to age of the oldest unprocessed task in event replication
queue (aka replication queue latency).

isArchived.description:
true if replication is archived. Archived replication will not generate or
sync new events. The main purpose of archived replication is to keep
replication metadata for future reference. Archived replication can be
safely deleted.

eventSource.description: How ongoing data change events are captured for this replication.

Represents specification and status of user-level or bucket-level
replication.

Selected user must be configured for both from/to storages.

Can be equal to from_storage if both from/to buckets are set and different.

For user-level replication, this field must be empty.
For bucket-level replication, this field must be set.

For user-level replication, this field must be empty.
For bucket-level replication, this field must be set. From/to buckets can
be different.

- Bucket-level  replicates a single bucket.

zeroDowntime.title: true if switch is zero downtime

multipartTtl.title: multipart uploads TTL for zero downtime switch

lastStartedAt.description:
Time of last switch attempt - last time when switch was moved to InProgress

doneAt.description: Time of last switch completion. Set only if switch status is Done.

chorusReplicationSwitchStatus.description:
- NOT_STARTED: Switch is not started yet
 - IN_PROGRESS: Switch is in progress. Draining replication events queue.
For switch with downtime, requests to target are blocked at this point.
 - CHECK_IN_PROGRESS: Switch is in progress. Queue is drained. Checking if source and
destination targets are the same. Requests are still blocked. Used only
for switch with downtime with enabled bucket check.
 - ERROR: Switch failed to complete in downtime window and was aborted.
Requests to target are unblocked. Used only for switch with downtime.
If cron downtime_window is used, switch will be retried on next cron
execution.
 - SKIPPED: Switch was not able to start in given downtime window because conditions
were not met. Used only for switch with downtime. If cron downtime_window
is used, switch will be retried on next cron execution.
 - DONE: Switch was successfully completed.
All data was replicated to replication destination target and all read
and all requests are now routed to it.

Optional. Server response date, used as reference timestamp when
Swift does not return Last-Modified (account/container/meta updates).

deleteMultipart.description: Optional. If true, indicates SLO/DLO multipart manifest deletion.

chorusSwiftOperation.description:
SwiftOperation determines which replication task is created.
Task handlers are idempotent — e.g. CONTAINER_UPDATE and CONTAINER_DELETE
both trigger a sync that compares source and destination state.

startOnInitDone.title:
If true, chorus will perform switch automatically when initial migration
will be done. Initial migration copies all objects that existed in source
bucket before replication started. default is false

cron.description:
If set, chorus will try or retry to start downtime window according to CRON
schedule.
It is not makes sense to set cron frequency less than one hour or less than
max_duration if used. Either cron or start_at can be set, but not both.

startAt.description:
If set, downtime window will be attempted at given time only once.
If at this point initial migration will not be done, switch will be marked
as failed and not executed. Either cron or start_at can be set, not both.

maxDuration.description:
If set, chorus will abort downtime window if it will not be able to
complete in given time. In this case, switch will be marked as failed and
will be retried on next cron execution if set.

maxEventLag.description:
If set, switch execution will be skipped if number of unprocessed events is
more than max_event_lag. Switch will be marked as failed and will be
retried on next cron execution if set.

skipBucketCheck.description:
if true, chorus will not perform equality check of target contents before
completing switch with downtime. Might be useful for buckets with large
number of objects. In this case check will consume a lot of time and memory
in Redis. Default is false.

continueReplication.description:
Set true to replicate data updates from new main to old main bucket after
successful switch. Default is false.

chorusSwitchDowntimeOpts.description:
Defines downtime window for replication switch with downtime.
All dates and times depends on local times of machine running chorus worker.
Time precision is ~1 minute.

replicationId.description:
Id of user- or bucket- level replication policy to switch source and
destination targets on proxy. Replication policy should already exist.
Agent-based replication is not supported.
Bucket-level replication with different from/to bucket names is not
supported.

downtimeOpts.description:
Configures downtime window for switch. During downtime all requests to
target will be blocked on proxy. If options are not set, downtime will be
started right away and will last until all replication tasks are processed.

with downtime window.

Bucket-level replication with different from/to bucket names is not

syncSkipped.description: Synchronous replication enabled but nothing to replicate synchronously for the request.

TrafficStats are cumulative in-memory traffic counters of one proxy instance.
For per-replication backlog (events, events_done, event_lag) use Policy/ListReplications.

bucket.description: bucket whose routing to change. Empty for the user-level routing.
